page_title: Optimize Options (Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC))

sources.section: Optimisation levels, inlining and link time
sources.entry: Options That Control Optimization (GCC) - Lists what each -O level turns on, the inlining limits, and that -Ofast admits transforms invalid for conforming code.

summary.title: Optimize Options (Using the GNU Compiler Collection)
summary.one_liner: You learn which optimization flags each GCC -O level (-O0, -O1, -O2, -O3, -Os, -Ofast, -Og, -Oz) enables, plus fine-grained flags like -finline-limit and -fno-inline.
takeaways: -O0 is the default and disables most optimization passes; -Og is suited to the edit-compile-debug cycle.
-O1 enables a base set of flags; -O2 adds nearly all non-space-speed-tradeoff passes; -O3 adds loop transforms and more cloning and unswitching.
-Os is -O2 minus flags that often grow code, plus size-focused tuning; -Oz is more aggressive about size.
-Ofast enables all -O3 optimizations plus ffast-math and other transforms that are invalid for some standard-compliant programs.
Use -Q --help=optimizers to see the exact set of optimizations enabled at each level on your target; the last -O option on the command line wins.
summary.summary: This GCC manual page lists the optimization flags turned on by each -O level and explains the trade-offs between compile time, code size, speed, and debuggability. It then documents individual fine-tuning flags such as -fomit-frame-pointer, -foptimize-crc, -ffp-contract, and the inlining controls (-finline-small-functions, -finline-functions, -finline-limit=n, -fno-inline). It is reference material rather than a tutorial, organized by level with per-flag descriptions.
